FINDING while testing 6637c75, and it's bigger than listens. The node's OWN subscribers take every arrival: puppetDoor, ownerPost.onArrival and boxes.onArrival are subscribed at startup (server.js:1372, 1403, 1407), so arrivals.note always counts a delivery and marks the row taken (arrivals.js:214). Measured on my node: 200 arrivals, 0 untaken, median 3 ms from arrival to taken. So the backlog replay (arrivals.js:121-151) never has anything to replay. Consequences: (1) an agents listener that is down loses those messages from its own log for good (they stay only in the node's traffic.jsonl); I told Andy the opposite and am correcting it. (2) Desk misses everything that arrives while Andy's browser is closed. listens covers only 'page open, Desk not mounted yet', and its backlog half never fires. A fix is a CORE gate (arrivals' delivery rule, or a node-side booted half for Desk), so it needs a shape for peer review plus Andy's yes. listens itself: I'll finish testing the page-open ordering, but it doesn't close the gap.

A correction to what I told you tonight: 'When it's down, nothing is lost' is WRONG. I measured it on my node: the node's own internal handlers (puppet door, owner post, boxes) collect every arriving message within milliseconds, so there's never a backlog held for a listener or page that isn't connected. What it means: while my listener is down, or your browser is closed, Desk's and the agents' own logs miss those messages. They stay only in the node's record. Fixing it touches the core's delivery rule, so claude-windows and I will bring it to you as a shape for your yes.

G1: every answer that goes out of a node obeys one size limit. Today nothing does. A verb that answers with a list just sends however much there is, so a big contact book or a long record could send more than a packet can carry. G1 puts one cap in limits.js, in bytes only and derived from MAX_PAYLOAD, and makes both ways an answer leaves (the page's door and the peer's packet) stop at it. It applies your rule 'Everything, everywhere that goes out, is bounded by MAX_PAYLOAD.' It sits right behind G2 because G2 builds the tool that does the cutting: getResult() on the bucket, which makes the byte-capped answer and sets 'more' when something was left out. Once G2 exists, G1 is putting that tool at both exits and proving nothing gets past it.

G17: the reply from an app has to make it back to the browser. For join, the invite IS the reply. Today the app server throws the reply body away (appServer.js:842), so a visitor on join.spirit.andyflinn.com could never receive their invite. The path is browser, then Caddy on the VPS, then appFaceApp on the VPS puppet node, then your node, then the join process, and back the same way. What you gave a go on is the first slice, the entry point on the VPS: a listener named puppetPost, after the page's lowest-level call, so both ends of that wire share one name. Caddy forwards to it, and it hands each request to appFaceApp and nothing else. It listens on loopback only, and relay-state/face.json switches it on. The node's own door stays loopback-only, so a visitor never reaches your node's verbs. It sits where it is because join, the whole alpha, is this path.
